examples.text: My little brother is such a sneak; yesterday I caught him trying to look through my diary.

glosses: The act of sneaking
A cheat; a con artist.

examples.text: I can't believe I gave that sneak $50 for a ticket when they were selling for $20 at the front gate.

glosses: An informer; a tell-tale.

A sneaker; a tennis shoe.

examples.text: We would have been laughed off the street in Philadelphia if we were seen wearing sneaks. In the big city, the young population wore loafers or boots.

Ellipsis of sneak preview

examples.text: At a "sneak preview," of course, the public is also on hand and can make their reactions felt much to the humiliation of the principals. At a sneak of "The Sandpiper," starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, the audience laughed so loud during one love scene that the dejected producer promptly cut the scene out of the picture. At a sneak of "The Outrage" in San Francisco it was decided not to give names at the outset to test public response: nearly half the audience left before the picture was 20 minutes old. […] The worst sneak, it is told, occurred one night when nearly the entire audience marched out on "Paris When It Sizzles” leaving the producer and director alone and forlorn in the theater.

glosses: To creep or go stealthily; to come or go while trying to avoid detection, as a person who does not wish to be seen.

examples.text: He decided to sneak into the kitchen for a second cookie while his mom was on the phone.
Some of these were dressed most gorgeously, others becomingly, and several sneaked in with fantail bangers, calling themselves "Gentlemen of the Nineteenth Century."

glosses: To take something stealthily without permission.

examples.text: I went to sneak a chocolate but my dad caught me.

glosses: To stealthily bring someone something.

examples.text: She asked me to sneak her a phone next month.

glosses: To hide, especially in a mean or cowardly manner.

examples.text: [Slander] sneaks its head.

glosses: To inform an authority of another's misdemeanours.

examples.text: If you sneak on me I'll bash you!

glosses: In advance; before release to the general public.

examples.text: The company gave us a sneak look at their new electronic devices.

glosses: In a stealthy or surreptitious manner.

examples.text: I was able to get a sneak peek at the guest list.

glosses: Arrastrarse suavemente, moverse con leve fricción sobre una superficie o a través de un medio denso como gases o líquidos.
tags: se emplea también como transitivo: deslizar

examples.text: El agua se desliza sobre la piel. El nadador se desliza por el agua con gracia.

glosses: Moverse con cautela, habilidad o pericia, en particular sin que otros lo noten.

examples.text: Los fugitivos se deslizaban por entre el bosque sin ser detectados.
¿O creías que no llegaría a conocer tu plan que se desliza astutamente, y que no me iba a defender si lo descubría?

glosses: Caerse algo, desprenderse de donde estaba.

examples.text: El vaso se le deslizó y se destrozó contra el suelo.

glosses: Desplazarse, especialmente un líquido, de manera fluida en cierta dirección.

examples.text: El río se desliza por el valle.

glosses: Experimentar una progresiva o paulatina conversión o transformación en ideas, actitudes, emociones o actividades.

examples.text: El político se deslizó hacia la derecha a medida que las presiones del gobierno aumentaron.

glosses: Cometer una falta o equivocación, especialmente moral, de modo total o parcialmente involuntario.
Se glisser.
